verdict.reasoning: Three papers (PreDAT, FlowSeq, EM Approach) directly solve the gap by proposing fully non-autoregressive models that generate all tokens in parallel, eliminating the left-to-right auto-regressive dependency. FlowSeq achieves near-constant decoding time; PreDAT delivers 17× throughput speedup; the EM approach provides theoretical grounding. Two partial-solution papers (Diffusion-NAT, InfoDiffusion) still use iterative refinement steps, but the direct solutions already demonstrate the core gap can be fully addressed. Remaining quality/coherence issues are limitations of specific NAR approaches, not of the dependency-reduction goal itself.

paper.title: Directed Acyclic Transformer Pre-training for High-quality Non-autoregressive Text Generation
paper.abstract: Non-AutoRegressive (NAR) text generation models have drawn much attention because of their significantly faster decoding speed and good generation quality in machine translation. However, in a wider range of text generation tasks, existing NAR models lack proper pre-training, making them still far behind the pre-trained autoregressive models. In this paper, we propose Pre-trained Directed Acyclic Transformer (PreDAT) and a novel pre-training task to promote prediction consistency in NAR generation. Experiments on five text generation tasks show that our PreDAT remarkably outperforms existing pre-trained NAR models (+4.2 scores on average) and even achieves better results than pre-trained autoregressive baselines in n-gram-based metrics, along with 17 times speedup in throughput. Further analysis shows that PreDAT benefits from the unbiased prediction order that alleviates the error accumulation problem in autoregressive generation, which provides new insights into the advantages of NAR generation.

assessments.contribution_summary: The paper proposes PreDAT (Pre-trained Directed Acyclic Transformer), a fully non-autoregressive text generation model that generates all tokens in parallel rather than sequentially. It introduces a novel pre-training task (Double-Source Text Infilling, DSTI) specifically designed for NAR generation, which promotes prediction consistency and bidirectional dependencies. The model achieves a 17x speedup in throughput over autoregressive models while maintaining competitive quality, and the paper explicitly demonstrates that NAR generation alleviates the error accumulation problem inherent in autoregressive generation due to its unbiased prediction order.
assessments.what_remains_open: The paper fully addresses the gap of reducing sequential auto-regressive dependency — it proposes a completely non-autoregressive model that predicts all tokens in parallel. However, the paper itself acknowledges remaining limitations of NAR generation (grammatical errors, long-range coherence issues) that are separate from the core gap of sequential dependency reduction. These are quality limitations of the specific approach, not a failure to address the gap itself.
evidence_snippets: Non-AutoRegressive (NAR) generation is an alternative text generation paradigm. Unlike sequential generation in AR models, NAR models predict all tokens in parallel, which largely accelerates the decoding process.
In contrast, NAR models naturally avoid the problem due to their unbiased prediction order.

paper.title: Diffusion-NAT: Self-Prompting Discrete Diffusion for Non-Autoregressive Text Generation
paper.abstract: Recently, continuous diffusion models (CDM) have been introduced into non-autoregressive (NAR) text-to-text generation. However, the discrete nature of text increases the difficulty of CDM to generate coherent and fluent texts, and also causes the incompatibility problem between CDM and advanced NLP techniques, especially the popular pre-trained language models~(PLMs). To solve it, we propose Diffusion-NAT, which introduces discrete diffusion models~(DDM) into NAR text-to-text generation and integrates BART to improve the performance. By revising the decoding process of BART and the typical settings of DDM, we unify the inference process of BART and the denoising process of DDM into the same NAR masked tokens recovering task. In this way, DDM can rely on BART to perform denoising, which can benefit from both the rich pre-learned knowledge of BART and the iterative refining paradigm of DDM. Besides, we also propose the iterative self-prompting strategy to further improve the generation quality. Experimental results on 7 datasets show that our approach can outperform competitive NAR methods, and even surpass autoregressive methods. Our code and data will be publicly released.

assessments.contribution_summary: The paper proposes Diffusion-NAT, a non-autoregressive (NAR) text generation model that uses discrete diffusion with BART to generate all tokens in parallel, reducing the auto-regressive dependency compared to standard AR models. It revises BART's decoding process from token-by-token to NAR masked token recovery, and uses iterative refinement across diffusion steps where each step is itself NAR. The method achieves strong results on multiple text generation benchmarks, outperforming other NAR methods and sometimes even AR methods.
assessments.what_remains_open: While the paper reduces auto-regressive dependency within each generation step (all tokens predicted in parallel), it introduces a different form of sequential dependency through the iterative denoising process across multiple diffusion steps. The model still requires multiple sequential refinement steps (e.g., 100 diffusion steps with DDIM) to achieve good quality, meaning generation is not fully parallelized in a single forward pass. The paper acknowledges this limitation explicitly: "An important limitation is the relatively higher inference latency of diffusion models." The gap of making generation fully non-sequential (single-shot parallel generation without iterative refinement) remains open. Additionally, the approach still relies on a pre-trained AR model (BART) as backbone, adapted to NAR use, rather than being a fundamentally non-sequential architecture.
evidence_snippets: We revise the decoding process of BART into the NAR manner that can recover all masked tokens simultaneously.
An important limitation is the relatively higher inference latency of diffusion models.
we can see that with very few diffusion steps (\eg 2 steps), our approach can also achieve a decent performance on BLEU-2 and Distinct-2.

paper.title: FlowSeq: Non-Autoregressive Conditional Sequence Generation with Generative Flow
paper.abstract: Most sequence-to-sequence (seq2seq) models are autoregressive; they generate each token by conditioning on previously generated tokens. In contrast, non-autoregressive seq2seq models generate all tokens in one pass, which leads to increased efficiency through parallel processing on hardware such as GPUs. However, directly modeling the joint distribution of all tokens simultaneously is challenging, and even with increasingly complex model structures accuracy lags significantly behind autoregressive models. In this paper, we propose a simple, efficient, and effective model for non-autoregressive sequence generation using latent variable models. Specifically, we turn to generative flow, an elegant technique to model complex distributions using neural networks, and design several layers of flow tailored for modeling the conditional density of sequential latent variables. We evaluate this model on three neural machine translation (NMT) benchmark datasets, achieving comparable performance with state-of-the-art non-autoregressive NMT models and almost constant decoding time w.r.t the sequence length.

assessments.contribution_summary: FlowSeq proposes a non-autoregressive sequence-to-sequence model that generates all output tokens in one parallel pass, eliminating the left-to-right autoregressive dependency. It uses generative flow to model expressive latent variables that capture interdependencies between target tokens, enabling the decoder to predict each token independently given the latent code and source. The model achieves almost constant decoding time with respect to sequence length, directly addressing the goal of making generation less sequential.
assessments.what_remains_open: The paper fully addresses the core gap of reducing auto-regressive sequential dependency in generation. However, some residual sequential aspects remain: (1) the model must predict target sequence length in advance, which is a sequential decision; (2) the flow architecture itself processes sequences with time-dependent operations; (3) performance still lags behind autoregressive models, suggesting that completely eliminating sequential dependencies may sacrifice quality; (4) the model uses approximate decoding methods (argmax, NPD, IWD) rather than exact inference over the joint distribution. These are limitations of the specific solution rather than an unaddressed part of the gap itself.
evidence_snippets: In this paper, we propose a simple, efficient, and effective model for non-autoregressive sequence generation using latent variable models.

FlowSeq is a flow-based sequence-to-sequence model, which is (to our knowledge) the first non-autoregressive seq2seq model utilizing generative flows. It allows for efficient parallel decoding while modeling the joint distribution of the output sequence.

As the decoder, we take the latent sequence z as input, run it through several layers of a neural sequence model such as a Transformer, then directly predict the output tokens in y individually and independently. Notably, unlike standard seq2seq decoders, we do not perform causal masking to prevent attending to future tokens, making the model fully non-autoregressive.

paper.title: An EM Approach to Non-autoregressive Conditional Sequence Generation
paper.abstract: Autoregressive (AR) models have been the dominating approach to conditional sequence generation, but are suffering from the issue of high inference latency. Non-autoregressive (NAR) models have been recently proposed to reduce the latency by generating all output tokens in parallel but could only achieve inferior accuracy compared to their autoregressive counterparts, primarily due to a difficulty in dealing with the multi-modality in sequence generation. This paper proposes a new approach that jointly optimizes both AR and NAR models in a unified Expectation-Maximization (EM) framework. In the E-step, an AR model learns to approximate the regularized posterior of the NAR model. In the M-step, the NAR model is updated on the new posterior and selects the training examples for the next AR model. This iterative process can effectively guide the system to remove the multi-modality in the output sequences. To our knowledge, this is the first EM approach to NAR sequence generation. We evaluate our method on the task of machine translation. Experimental results on benchmark data sets show that the proposed approach achieves competitive, if not better, performance with existing NAR models and significantly reduces the inference latency.

assessments.contribution_summary: This paper directly addresses the goal of reducing sequential auto-regressive dependency in generation by proposing a novel Expectation-Maximization (EM) framework for training Non-Autoregressive (NAR) sequence generation models. NAR models generate all output tokens in parallel (removing the sequential dependency of AR models), and the paper's EM approach jointly optimizes both an AR teacher and a NAR student in a closed loop to overcome the multi-modality problem that typically limits NAR model accuracy. The paper provides theoretical analysis showing NAR models can be universal approximators when multi-modality is removed, and empirically demonstrates that their approach achieves competitive accuracy with significantly reduced inference latency on machine translation benchmarks.
assessments.what_remains_open: The paper fully addresses the gap of reducing sequential auto-regressive dependency. It proposes and evaluates a method (NAR models trained via EM) that generates all output tokens in parallel, directly tackling the core problem. The paper acknowledges that NAR models still face challenges (e.g., word duplication, multi-modality) but provides concrete solutions for these within the NAR paradigm. No part of the "less sequential generation" goal remains unaddressed by this paper — it is a direct solution to that very problem.
evidence_snippets: Non-autoregressive (NAR) models have been recently proposed to reduce the latency by generating all output tokens in parallel
This formulation allows each token to be decoded in parallel and hence brings a significant reduction of the inference latency.
Experimental results on benchmark data sets show that the proposed approach achieves competitive, if not better, performance with existing NAR models and significantly reduces the inference latency.

paper.title: InfoDiffusion: Information Entropy Aware Diffusion Process for Non-Autoregressive Text Generation
paper.abstract: Diffusion models have garnered considerable interest in the field of text generation. Several studies have explored text diffusion models with different structures and applied them to various tasks, including named entity recognition and summarization. However, there exists a notable disparity between the "easy-first" text generation process of current diffusion models and the "keyword-first" natural text generation process of humans, which has received limited attention. To bridge this gap, we propose InfoDiffusion, a non-autoregressive text diffusion model. Our approach introduces a "keyinfo-first" generation strategy and incorporates a noise schedule based on the amount of text information. In addition, InfoDiffusion combines self-conditioning with a newly proposed partially noising model structure. Experimental results show that InfoDiffusion outperforms the baseline model in terms of generation quality and diversity, as well as exhibiting higher sampling efficiency.

assessments.contribution_summary: InfoDiffusion proposes a non-autoregressive text diffusion model that uses an information-entropy-aware noise schedule to prioritize generating high-information-content words first ("keyinfo-first" strategy), combined with self-conditioning and partial noising. The model is inherently non-autoregressive (generating tokens in parallel via diffusion), which addresses the goal of reducing sequential dependency. The paper's specific contribution is improving the generation order within an already non-autoregressive diffusion framework to better match human-like generation patterns.
assessments.what_remains_open: The paper does not propose a general method for converting auto-regressive models into less-sequential ones; it starts from an already non-autoregressive diffusion model and improves its quality and efficiency. The gap of "reducing auto-regressive dependency" more broadly encompasses approaches that could make existing auto-regressive models less sequential (e.g., through insertion-based, masked, or iterative refinement methods), whereas this paper focuses on improving a specific non-autoregressive diffusion architecture. Additionally, the paper does not address how to reduce sequential dependency in other types of generation models (e.g., transformer-based auto-regressive LMs) or provide a general framework applicable beyond diffusion-based text generation.
evidence_snippets: Non-autoregressive (NAR) generation refers to a method of generating sequences where each element is generated independently, without relying on previously generated elements, allowing for faster parallel generation but potentially sacrificing the generation accuracy

Experimental results show that InfoDiffusion outperforms the baseline model in terms of generation quality and diversity, as well as exhibiting higher sampling efficiency.
